editorial:
Imagine waking up with guns bolted to your hands and a deadly game hunting you down. That is the wild ride you get with Guns Akimbo. Daniel Radcliffe plays Miles, a normal guy who spends his nights trolling a violent streaming website. When the site's owners decide to make him their next star, they bolt pistols to his hands and force him into a fight to the death against Nix, a fierce and heavily armed killer played by Samara Weaving. The movie mixes dark humor with nonstop action, throwing you into a neon-soaked world where every moment feels like a video game gone wrong. It is loud, silly, and surprisingly fun.

The action scenes are fast and creative, and Radcliffe sells the panic and pain of a guy who cannot even scratch his nose. Weaving steals every scene she is in with wild energy. The pacing rarely slows down, which keeps things exciting, though the humor can feel over the top at times. If you enjoy chaotic action comedies, this one is a blast.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Nix turns against the website's boss Riktor and sacrifices herself to save Miles. Miles, still stuck with guns on his hands, uses his wits and the weapons to take down Riktor and his crew. With the game shut down and the website destroyed, Miles survives and walks away free. He finally gets the guns removed and reunites with his ex-girlfriend Nova, ready to move on with a normal life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves chaotic action comedies and video-game-style thrills.
